quote.text: We often are angry," says our adversary, "not with men who have hurt us, but with men who are going to hurt us: so you may be sure that anger is not born of injury.
quote.author: Seneca
quote.aiInsight:
• Parenthood:
    • Recognize that anger towards your children often stems from fear of their future mistakes rather than their present actions; cultivate patience by focusing on guiding rather than reacting.
    • Embrace each moment as an opportunity to teach through calm presence, acknowledging that emotional reactions may forecast worries about anticipated challenges rather than actual missteps.
  • Leadership:
    • Understand that your anger towards team members is sometimes a mirror of your own anxieties about potential failures; turn this insight into a drive for proactive problem-solving.
    • Lead by example through self-mastery and measured responses, ensuring that you address issues based on facts rather than projections of future harm.
  • Product Management:
    • Realize that anger in the product arena often originates from fears about upcoming market challenges or anticipated setbacks; use it as a signal to delve deeper into strategic planning.
    • Channel your emotions into constructive insights by examining underlying assumptions and risks, enabling you to make reasoned decisions rather than reactive judgments.
